scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

P-M2C.name: meter-to-cash
steps: read collection (AMI interval read or field manual read)
estimate substitution when no accepted read

DA-MDMS.name: MDMS AMI read event log (system of record for AMI reads)

DA-RULES.name: billing import validation rule change log

F-01.statement: Dispute volume monthly: June 2026 = 610, July = 590, August = 1180, September = 1260

F-02.statement: Tariff change log contains zero records.

F-03.statement: Route completion for Aug‑Sep 2026 is 0.88 with 9,200 manual read accounts, below the 0.95 target.

F-05.statement: Dispute response times: median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days, SLA 3.0 days, total tickets 2440.

F-06.statement: Among disputed estimated bills, 1184 AMI reads were taken before cutoff and rejected due to high consumption, while 56 had no read received.

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

CL-03.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-04.statement: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

H-REQUESTER-FRAMING.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August; the root cause is unknown billing errors that an AI agent can fix.

H-AMI-READ-FAILURE.statement: AMI meter read delivery failures or delays cause estimation substitution, leading to incorrect bills and disputes.

H-FIELD-READ-ERROR.statement: Contracted field staffing issues or route execution errors cause missed or erroneous manual reads, leading to estimate substitution and wrong bills.

H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE.statement: Recent changes to billing import validation rules have introduced bugs that misapply tariffs or read types, generating incorrect bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The dispute ticket count rose from ~600 per month in June‑July to >1180 in August and 1260 in September, confirming roughly a doubling since August.
The tariff change log shows no recorded tariff changes, indicating that tariff modifications are not a source of recent billing discrepancies.
Route completion for August‑September is 0.88, below the 0.95 target, indicating field meter‑read execution fell short and may have led to estimation substitution and higher dispute volume.

The observation shows that among disputed bills, more are associated with actual reads (1785) than estimated reads (1240), indicating that disputes are not driven primarily by estimation substitution.

E-05.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The stakeholder reports a shortage of three field readers since July, causing routes to run late and resulting in estimated bills for affected customers.

Dispute ticket response times are within the service level agreement (median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days < 3 days SLA) with 2,440 tickets processed, indicating the dispute handling process meets its response targets and delayed response is not a likely driver of the dispute volume surge.

E-07.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The stakeholder states there has been no tariff change this year, indicating that tariff modifications are not a source of the recent billing discrepancy surge.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The service contract confirms that the utility can request route priority changes, but only after confirmation by the Field Operations Manager, aligning with existing runtime confirmation requirements for route changes.

E-09.content: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

interpretation_history.interpretation: MDMS export access is now provisioned, allowing retrieval of AMI read event data for further investigation; it does not by itself indicate whether AMI reads are failing or causing disputes.

The observation shows that for disputed estimated bills, the majority of AMI reads were taken before the billing cutoff but were rejected due to high consumption, while a small fraction had no read received. This indicates that AMI reads are being delivered but are being blocked by validation rules, suggesting a billing import issue rather than missing reads.

problem_definition.requested_solution: Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.
problem_definition.root_problem: Dispute ticket volume has doubled since August due to incorrect bills caused by recent billing import validation rule changes that misapply tariffs or read types.

trace.summary: Dispute ticket volume has doubled since August due to incorrect bills caused by recent billing import validation rule changes that misapply tariffs or read types.

details.requested_solution: Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

structural_remedies.description: Revert billing import validation rules to the pre‑August known‑good version and institute a change‑control process requiring automated unit‑test validation and stakeholder sign‑off before any rule modification.
structural_remedies.rationale: Audit and rollback of rule changes can be completed within the remaining 225 minutes; does not involve automated bill writes or field‑dispatch changes, so complies with K‑BILLWRITE and K‑DISPATCH.; residual gap: Route completion remains at 0.88 (below the 0.95 target); may still generate some estimation‑related disputes, but evidence shows disputes are not primarily estimation‑driven (E‑04).

structural_remedies.description: Add a pre‑deployment validation step that compares rule‑set outputs against a sandbox of recent bills to catch mis‑applications before promotion to production.
structural_remedies.rationale: Implementing a sandbox check can be done within the remaining time and does not violate any authority or human‑approval constraints.; residual gap: Same as R1 – route completion gap remains; however, the primary bug source is eliminated.

solution_design.bridge_sunset_condition: If the billing import validation rule changes are not reverted to the pre-August known-good version within the remaining contest time (225 minutes), then the agent's automated dispute response shall be suspended and manual handling resumed.

proposal.summary: Dispute ticket volume has doubled since August due to incorrect bills caused by recent billing import validation rule changes that misapply tariffs or read types.
key_points: Problem: Dispute ticket volume has doubled since August due to incorrect bills caused by recent billing import validation rule changes that misapply tariffs or read types. [E-01, E-10]

Establishment: We observed the dispute ticket count rise from ~600 to >1180 per month (E-01), found disputed bills are more often linked to actual reads than estimated reads (E-04), and saw that most AMI reads for disputed estimated bills were taken before the cutoff but rejected due to high consumption (E-10), indicating a billing import validation issue rather than missing reads or tariff changes (E-02).
Release: The release includes validation of dispute ticket classification using CRM ticket data (DA-TICKET) and verification of AMI read integrity using MDMS export data (DA-MDMS).

Decision rationale: The release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION because core verification passed but the release scope does not yet audit the billing import validation rule changes identified as the root cause (semantic:addresses_root_problem limitation), and items such as VOB-U-U1 remain deferred, resulting in a conditional pass.
